content:
I am currently working towards defining the continuous/discontinuous decomposition of a local martingale in order to define the stochastic integral, and to do that I defined the Hilbert space structure of square integrable martingales. For that I used the fact that any local martingale has a càdlàg modification (as a sorry), but I need the modification to be a martingale as well.

Because MeasureTheory.Martingale requires strong measurability however, a modification of a martingale is not necessarily a martingale (see MeasureTheory.Martingale.congr which requires strong measurability).

Therefore I think we should redefine Martingale to only require a.e. strong measurability. I don't know if that could cause serious breaks but as conditional expectation is only defined a.e. I think this should go fine. Thoughts?
(Actually being a martingale is not even preserved by indistinguishability)
Maybe there will be some problems when you consider stopping times of a martingale: StronglyAdapted.isStoppingTime_leastGE

Also just to note that if you want to make this change you only need to delete StronglyAdapted from the definition of martingale as AEStronglyMeasurable is already implied by μ[f j | ℱ i] =ᵐ[μ] f i and stronglyMeasurable_condExp (actually this is also how Martingale.integrable is proved)
Hmmm maybe we need to redefine stopping times via null measurability as well then?
Although IsStoppingTime does not depend on a measure rn
Isn't the cadlag modification of a strongly measurable martingale also strongly measurable as well?

I expect it is yes, this was just the start of my question but I don’t think this particular case will be an issue. But I was asking more generally because (as we often do in mathlib) we deal with modifications without caring about measurability and relying on a.e. measurability but here we cannot do that and that disturbed me.
